key_insight: Imperfect physics improves regression convergence rates only below a modeling-error threshold; with exact physics, studied PDE classes yield rates corresponding to dimension d−1 rather than d.
engineering_relevance: The results clarify when PDE constraints can improve statistical performance beyond smoothness alone and give conditions for near-linear estimator computation.
method: Benchmark physics-informed regression against optimal regression using only smoothness.
Derive modeling-error thresholds for all linear PDEs and certain nonlinear PDEs.
Establish rates for constant-coefficient elliptic and hyperbolic PDE classes and tune hyperparameters without knowing the modeling error.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence guarantees and minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors, not empirical dataset evaluations.
watch_item: The detailed rate improvements apply to specified PDE classes, and near-linear computation requires additional conditions.
paper_title: Minimax Rates for imperfect Physics-Informed Regression
